summary: Router 0.29.0 (ADR-0089, proposed): a recall skipped because the request carries tools (ADR-0059) is also recorded as a run per client in the new module recall_skips.py, called from memory.prepare after scope_for, keyed by the authenticated principal. /admin/context (control port, basic_auth_middleware on every route) lists the runs with client, project, since, last and request count; the Overview renders them with textContent. A gauge without labels counts the clients, and one warning line per run (at most one per client and hour) gives only a count, no client or project, following the memory logging rule. Traced: memory.prepare (the tools check and the recall decision are unchanged, the recall is still skipped; passed() is called only after the check), the control app middleware, context_ops.snapshot and its callers (handle, metrics.render), and the UI rendering. Memory is bounded by the configured principals, because only requests that passed scope_for reach the tracking. No request content reaches the state, the log or the metric. The project name in a run is a granted project of that client. The log's next step names recall_into_tools: true together with the risk it accepts (TM-10) and does not change policy. No finding was introduced.

limitations: The per-client state is in memory only; after a restart a client is reported again only with its next skipped request.
The Overview tile was not checked in a browser; it uses textContent only and selftest_browser's static checks pass.
A client deliberately working with tools and without recall is listed too (at most one log line per hour); this is documented, not suppressed.
